Test Objective: Verify PCIe device enumeration by performing link training, cache coherency programming, link status polling, vendor ID read, command register configuration, memory base programming, BAR enumeration on both DM0 and DM1 instances, and synchronization handshake.
Test Description: This test validates the complete PCIe device enumeration flow. It begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training on the configured PCIe instance (DM0 or DM1 in RC or EP mode). Cache coherency control is then programmed on both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances by setting the master AXI read/write cache mode and value fields via read-modify-write operations on the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register. The test polls the SII link status registers on both instances until the link is confirmed up (status bits 0xD1). In RC mode, the Vendor ID is read from the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG is configured to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master access, and memory base programming is performed for both DM0 and DM1. System-level configuration registers are then written. Cache coherency is subsequently disabled by clearing the cache value fields. BAR enumeration is performed on both slave interfaces by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0_REG through PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, reading back to determine BAR sizes, then programming final BAR values. The test concludes by polling the synchronization register for a completion handshake value of 0x12345678.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. The compile-time mode flag (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP) is defined.
4. System integration interface (SII) registers are accessible.
5. PCIe DBI and slave configuration spaces are accessible.
6. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x0 to the synchronization register (0xE6004100) to initialize the handshake.
2. Perform PCIe link training on the configured instance (DM0 or DM1) with x4 lane width.
3. Program cache coherency on PCIE0 instance: read COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, set AXI write cache mode bits [14:11] to 0xF and read cache mode bits [6:3] to 0xF via read-modify-write, then set AXI write cache value bits [30:27] to 0xF and read cache value bits [22:19] to 0xF.
4. Repeat cache coherency programming for PCIE1 instance.
5. Wait for 20 cycles, then perform a consolidated cache coherency write on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
6. Poll SII0 link status register (0xC0) until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC programming.
8. Poll SII1 link status register (0xC0) until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
9. In RC mode: Read TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG (0x0) to retrieve the Vendor ID.
10. In RC mode: Write 0x7 to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG (0x4) to enable IO Space, Memory Space, and Bus Master.
11. In RC mode: Execute memory base programming for DM0 and DM1 instances.
12. Write 0x1 to six system-level configuration registers (0xE690000C-0xE6900034).
13. Disable cache coherency on PCIE0: clear AXI cache value bits while keeping mode bits.
14. Repeat cache disable on PCIE1.
15. Perform BAR enumeration on slave interface 1: write 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0_REG(0x10) through PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG(0x24), read back, then program final BAR values.
16. Repeat BAR enumeration on slave interface 0.
17. Poll synchronization register (0xE6004100) until value 0x12345678 is received.
18. Call finish(0) to end the test.
Expected Results:
1. Link training completes successfully.
2. Cache coherency fields are correctly programmed and verified on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
3. SII0 and SII1 link status registers report link-up status (bits matching 0xD1).
4. Vendor ID read returns expected value (0x16C3 per spec reset value).
5. Command register is successfully written with IO, Memory, and Bus Master enable bits.
6. Memory base programming completes without errors.
7. System-level configuration registers accept writes.
8. Cache coherency is successfully disabled on both instances.
9. BAR enumeration returns valid BAR size information.
10. Final BAR address values are programmed and read back correctly.
11. Synchronization register reaches 0x12345678.
12. Test completes with finish(0) indicating PASS.

Functional Area: PCIe DMA Write and Read Data Transfer
Test Objective: Verify PCIe DMA write and read data transfer across all 4 channels (CH0-CH3) on both DM0 and DM1 instances, including interrupt-driven completion, doorbell triggering, and interrupt status/clear handling.
Test Description: This test validates PCIe DMA write and read operations across all four DMA channels. It begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training. The SII link status is polled until link-up is confirmed. In RC mode, the Vendor ID is read, the command register is configured, and BAR/memory base programming is performed. Data is preloaded into source memory with patterns 0xC0DEBEED and 0xF00DDEAF. GIC interrupt handling is set up. DMA write interrupt masks are cleared on the target instance. For each of the 4 write channels (CH0-CH3), the DMA write channel is programmed and the write doorbell register is triggered. The test waits for interrupt-driven completion via the Default_IRQHandler. After all write channels complete, the same sequence is performed for all 4 read channels (CH0-CH3) using the read doorbell register. The IRQ handler reads DMA write/read interrupt status registers, clears interrupts via the interrupt clear registers, and acknowledges the GIC. The test completes with finish(0).
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. The compile-time mode flag (DM0_RC or DM1_RC) is defined.
4. GIC interrupt controller is functional.
5. DMA engine is available with 4 write and 4 read channels.
6. Source and destination memory regions are accessible.
7. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x0 to synchronization register (0xE6004100).
2. Perform link training on configured instance (DM0 or DM1) with x4 lane width.
3. Poll SII link status register (0xC0) until link-up (0xD1) is confirmed.
4. Read Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG (0x0).
5. Write 0x7 to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG (0x4) to enable IO, Memory, Bus Master.
6. Execute BAR programming and memory base programming.
7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC.
8. Poll synchronization register (0xE6004100) until value 0x12345678.
9. Preload source memory at 0xE6000000 with 128 words of 0xC0DEBEED and 128 words of 0xF00DDEAF.
10. Initialize GIC interrupt handling (GIC_Set, GIC_EnableAllIRQ).
11. Write 0x0 to DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF to unmask write interrupts.
12. Write 0x0 to DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF to unmask read interrupts.
13. Program DMA write channel 0 and write 0x0 to DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF.
14. Wait for interrupt completion (int_pend cleared by IRQ handler).
15. Repeat steps 13-14 for write channels 1 (doorbell=0x1), 2 (doorbell=0x2), 3 (doorbell=0x3).
16. Program DMA read channel 0 and write 0x0 to DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF.
17. Wait for interrupt completion.
18. Repeat steps 16-17 for read channels 1 (doorbell=0x1), 2 (doorbell=0x2), 3 (doorbell=0x3).
19. In IRQ handler: Read DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF, mask with 0x0000000F.
20. In IRQ handler: Read DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF, mask with 0x0000000F.
21. In IRQ handler: Write to DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF to clear write interrupts.
22. In IRQ handler: Write to DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF to clear read interrupts.
23. In IRQ handler: Call GIC_ClearIRQ to acknowledge interrupt.
24. Call finish(0) to end test.

2. SII link status reports link-up (0xD1).
3. Vendor ID read returns expected value.
4. Command register write is accepted.
5. DMA write interrupt masks are cleared (0x0 written to DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF).
6. DMA read interrupt masks are cleared (0x0 written to DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF).
7. All 4 DMA write channels complete with interrupt-driven confirmation.
8. DMA write doorbell triggers transfer for each channel.
9. All 4 DMA read channels complete with interrupt-driven confirmation.
10. DMA read doorbell triggers transfer for each channel.
11. IRQ handler correctly reads DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF.
12. IRQ handler correctly clears interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF.
13. Test completes with finish(0) indicating PASS.
